newsitem.title: UK: UK CBI gives qualified support to business report.
newsitem.headline: UK CBI gives qualified support to business report.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry gave its qualified support on Tuesday to a report by business leaders whose recommendations closely follow many of the opposition Labour Party's economic policies.
The CBI praised the report, commissioned by the left-of-centre Institute for Public Policy and Research, for showing that a consensus was emerging on how to improve Britain's economic performance.

CBI director general Adair Turner agreed with many of the report's recommendations, such as reform of competition policy and investment in education, but disagreed with its call for a minimum wage and for Britain to sign up to the European Union's Social Chapter.
Turner said the report correctly identified problems which had held back the British economy, including low investment, underperforming firms and underperforming people.
He supported its view that market deregulation in Britain was not enough on its own to promote prosperity and agreed with the report's conclusions on short-termism and low investment.
But he said the CBI had some different assessments on the severity of the problem and on some of the policy responses. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
